notes:
Short summary: Sentinel Atlas is a federal defense research org evaluating a RAG-based secure search to index large classified corpora (historical ops reports, sensor logs, PDFs, email archives). Primary focus = embeddings + reranking pipeline (ANN index + reranker model) for high-precision retrieval under strict latency constraints. They must run on-prem in an air-gapped enclave.

What they told us: "we need 95th percentile query latency <200ms for top-5 reranked results at 50 qps across 50M documents; cost per query is secondary to reliability but must be predictable for budget forecasting". They are sensitive to model provenance and want open-model stack that can be audited (weights stored on-prem).

Security posture: require SSO/SAML via internal IdP, KMS/HSM integration, full audit logs with retention controls, FIPS-validated crypto, FedRAMP guidance. ATO/Authority to Operate is mandatory before production. They will not accept hosted inference with egress.

Procurement notes: long procurement cycle — must go through PMO and enterprise contracting. They asked for sample SOW, security FAQ, and a government-friendly pricing template. Legal flagged indemnity and data handling clauses.

Sales tone: cautious but positive. AE/SE impression: high technical comprehension, procurement-heavy, multi-stakeholder (security, infra, PMO, contracting).
requirements_summary: Indexing scale: target initial corpus 50M documents (300M+ passages), growth expectation 3x/yr. Embedding footprint: offline bulk embed pipeline with GPU nodes; vector index on-prem using FAISS/ANN with sharding. Reranker: small transformer reranker to re-score top-100 retrieval set, latency budget 120ms reranker + retrieval combined at 95th. Throughput: baseline 50 qps, burst to 200 qps during exercises. Cost sensitivity: mid-to-high (government budgeted) but need predictable ARR and capital procurement (CapEx for on-prem HW).
procurement_notes: Requested artifacts: SOO/SOW template, SOC2 + FedRAMP artifacts, FIPS crypto proofs, sample acceptance criteria for POC, pricing in GSA-friendly format. Procurement timeline: internal review Mar-Apr, PMO approval May, contracting June-July. Decision drivers: security compliance, demonstrable latency at scale, clear runbook for upgrades, rollback and fallback strategies.
